claims.statement: Local dev/test infrastructure is split into four independently operable named Compose stacks — auth, mcm, audit and observability — each its own Compose project defined by a thin `include:`-only aggregator under `infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/`, and each brought up and down through its own Nx lifecycle target (`up-auth`/`up-mcm`/`up-audit`/`up-observability`/`up-all`/`up-mcm-agents` and the `down-*` counterparts) rather than a bare `docker compose` invocation; the former single root compose.yaml aggregator is retired to a pointer.

`node scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs` mints one gitignored `infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/<stack>.env` per stack from the committed `<stack>.env.example` templates; it is idempotent (`--force` rotates, `--stack=<name>` scopes) and it COMPLETES an existing file rather than skipping it: keys the template has gained since are seeded INTO the existing `<stack>.env` (otherwise delivering one new variable would require `--force`, which rotates every other running value), and item #552 extends the same rule to a `<generate:KIND>` key that is present but EMPTY (`KEY=`) — minted in place, because it holds no value so filling it rotates nothing, whereas counting it as present made the run say up to date while the suite needing it skipped to green. A blank key that is NOT a `<generate:KIND>` placeholder is left untouched — the generator has no value to give it — and since the `REGISTRY_HOST=` entries left `mcm.env.example` and `observability.env.example` with feature 080, that branch survives only against the guard test's synthetic template. Deterministic fixtures (the LangFuse init keys, the `BACKUP_TEST_*` public halves) are copied verbatim even under `--force`. Each seeded run prints the key NAMES it added or filled — never values — and warns that containers started before the run do not hold the new values, so the consuming containers must be recreated and `gen-dev-env.mjs` re-run. Exit codes: `0` success · `1` missing/malformed template, unknown generation kind, or unwritable output · `2` bad args.

Every credential in the four stacks is externalized out of the tracked Compose files, but fail-fast `${VAR:?…}` interpolation is NOT universal: most secrets are that form, while the BFF (`bff/compose.yaml`) and web-api-mcp (`web-api-mcp/compose.yaml`) load their whole environment from a file with `env_file:` (`frontend/mcm-app/.env.docker` and `mcp-servers/web-api-mcp/.env.local` respectively), and the agent gateway keeps `AGENT_GATEWAY_CLIENT_SECRET` as an optional `${…:-}` so it can start without token exchange. `<stack>.env` is gitignored while `<stack>.env.example` is tracked through a `!infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.env.example` carve-out scoped to that directory so other deliberately ignored templates stay ignored, and `scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs` runs in the guardrails workflow's `naming` job both as `--selftest` (proving the detector flags a planted literal, including an inline `${VAR:-default}`) and as the real scan over the tracked compose files, failing the build if a literal credential is re-inlined.

It is the `up-auth` Nx target — not `gen-dev-env.mjs` — that seeds the dev Keycloak realm: `up-auth` applies the `keycloak/compose.dev.yaml` overlay as a second `-f` on top of the shared keycloak base, adding `--import-realm` plus a mount of the placeholder-only `dev-realm.json` whose `${…}` client secrets and test-user password Keycloak resolves from `stacks/auth.env` at import, so a from-scratch box gets the realm, its app clients and the seeded test user with no manual import; the import is non-destructive (Keycloak skips a realm that already exists), so an established `keycloak-store-postgres-data` volume is untouched and wiping the volume re-seeds on the next `up-auth`. `gen-dev-env.mjs` then projects those same auth.env secrets into the BFF env files, giving realm-secret == BFF-secret by construction, and because the projector legitimately runs before `up-auth` a first run on a fresh box ends `NOT verified` and is re-run after the realm is up.

Item #227: `backend/mc-service/.env.local` had no generator, so `pnpm nx affected -t lint,test,typecheck` on a branch whose Rust tree was byte-identical to main reported `mc-service:test` FAILED with 16 of 41 cases failing on configuration (`Missing("MC_DB_URL")`) rather than code. `gen-dev-env.mjs` now creates the file when absent, re-syncs the KEYCLOAK_*/E2E_* lines from stacks/auth.env, and seeds MC_DB_URL, MC_SERVICE_PORT and RUST_LOG once and never rewrites them, taking that binary to 41 passed / 0 failed.

The four E2E_* variables in `backend/mc-service/.env.local` (used by feature 046's authenticated `http_authz_test::*` cases to mint a real ROPC token) were the second half of item #227 and had been wrongly recorded as nine genuine replica-set-MongoDB failures: measured 2026-09-15 with Mongo up and the other 32 cases passing, all nine failed on `E2E_ROPC_CLIENT_ID is not set (or is empty)` instead.

`auth` must be brought up before the `mcm` stack's `app` profile because Docker Compose has no cross-project `depends_on`, so the ordering is manual — but the failure mode is 401s, not a hang: mc-service does not wait for Keycloak (`axum-keycloak-auth` runs OIDC discovery and the JWKS fetch in a background task while the service binds and serves immediately), so with Keycloak down or unreachable the service still starts and `/health` answers while every protected request is rejected with 401. This is pinned by `unauthenticated_401_is_returned_even_when_keycloak_is_unreachable` in the mc-service integration tier.

A password-on-first-init credential (Postgres, OpenSearch) is baked into its data volume on first boot and ignores later env changes, so rotating one for real requires regenerating the `.env` with `--force` AND recreating the service against a fresh volume; otherwise the container keeps the volume's original password and authentication fails with nothing pointing at the cause. Redis values, Unleash tokens and app secrets have no such persistence and rotate on a plain restart, and RustFS is in that second group rather than the first (feature 080): it does not bake its key pair into the drive — measured by starting it on a migrated drive with a different pair, which the new pair could read and the old pair could not — so rotating `LANGFUSE_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY` or `BACKUP_TEST_S3_SECRET_KEY` is an `.env` change plus recreating every consumer of that key, with no volume touched. Recreating the store alone is not enough, because one Langfuse key reaches four services in `observability/compose.yaml`: the two S3 upload key pairs on `langfuse-web` and `langfuse-worker` (through a shared environment anchor), the `langfuse-rustfs` server, and the `langfuse-rustfs-init` bucket one-shot. On the backup side the pair reaches `mcm-bff-backup-rustfs` and its bucket-init one-shot — and also the host-side backup suites, which read the value out of `frontend/mcm-app/.env.local`, the file `gen-dev-env.mjs` re-projects from `stacks/mcm.env` on every run, so the generator must be re-run after a rotation.

`docker compose down --volumes` wipes only transient volumes: every persistent data volume is declared `external: true` with an explicit name in its own service compose file (so the stack's `include:` merge does not prefix it with the project name) and therefore survives, so wiping real data requires removing the external volumes by hand after `down`.
With Docker Compose v2 a `--profile` flag must precede the `up`/`down` subcommand — placed after it the flag is silently ignored.

The `mcm` stack's heavy `--profile agents` variant (gateway + three MCP servers + a Postgres checkpointer) needs its Keycloak client secret fetched live from a running Keycloak because there is no committed source for it; without it the gateway starts but every tool call fails closed (chat works, add/query/organize do not). `pnpm nx up-mcm-agents infrastructure-as-code` performs that fetch-and-inject, and is distinct from `scripts/agent-stack.mjs`, the light E2E variant using `docker run` with an in-memory checkpointer.

A credential-driven integration-test skip means a missing gitignored file, not an unrunnable box: on 2026-08-07 an absent `frontend/mcm-app/.env.local` produced 38 errors and the wrong conclusion that the leg could only be proven in CI, because `syncEnvFile` returned early on a missing file so the three realm client secrets reached `.env.docker` but never the file `kc_admin.cfg()` reads; one `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` run took the suite from 13 passed / 38 errors to 51 passed / 0 failed.

The feature-048 lesson generalizes: before concluding 'this cannot run in this environment', name the specific missing input and check whether a generator, a `.env` file or a documented command supplies it — and a credential skip that does not name the variable, the file it is read from and the command that fixes it is itself the bug. Secrets are therefore checked by key name only (`cut -d= -f1`), never by printing a value.

The absences that remain legitimate in a healthy local run are the services behind profiles `app-e2e` does not select: `--profile observability` (LangFuse, otel-lgtm, Unleash and OPA), `--profile audit` (OpenSearch) and `--profile vault`. The dev-mode Vault is not an observability service — feature 020 relocated it into the `auth` stack under the `vault` profile — so looking for it under `up-observability` is itself the mistake; those skips are expected and allow-listed, and the healthy baseline for the agent integration suite is 51 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed.

Item #395: `gen-dev-env.mjs` asks the running realm for a token with each projected credential (`client_credentials` for `mcm-bff-service`, ROPC for `mcm-bff-test`) BEFORE writing anything, and reports one of four endings — `VERIFIED against the realm` (files written, exit 0), `NOT verified` on an unreachable realm or HTTP 404/5xx (files written, equality not claimed, exit 0), `NOT verified (MCM_SKIP_REALM_VERIFY is set)` (files written, exit 0), or `REFUSING TO WRITE: the realm … rejects credential(s)` (files untouched, exit 2).

The verify-before-write ordering is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: measured on the operator's box 2026-09-09, `auth.env`'s `E2E_ROPC_CLIENT_SECRET` was the stale side while a hand-corrected `.env.e2e.local` held the value the realm actually accepts, so a generator that wrote first and checked afterwards would have destroyed the only working credential on the machine before announcing the problem.

The remedy for a stale projected credential depends on how much drift there is, and drift must be measured before acting: `stacks/auth.env` stays the source of truth (it seeds the realm) so the fix belongs at the realm, never by copying the realm's secret back into an env file. Measured 2026-09-09 on this repository, five of six client secrets matched `auth.env` and only `mcm-bff-test` had been regenerated — so the tempting reading 'the realm was seeded from a different auth.env' was wrong and the volume wipe it implies would have destroyed the whole Keycloak database to correct one field. A few drifted clients are converged via the admin API; most or all drifting means a real re-seed.

`MCM_SKIP_REALM_VERIFY=1` makes `gen-dev-env.mjs` project anyway, knowing the files will carry credentials the realm refuses; it is the escape hatch for an unusual realm and not a fix, and the run announces the skip rather than quietly restoring the old unconditional equality claim.

`frontend/mcm-app/.env.e2e.local` is deliberately NOT auto-created, because its sync set is only the credential half and the web E2E also needs hand-maintained fixture keys, so a created file would be half-written; absence is instead reported as a loud warning that the web E2E will fail to log in, with the keys to add.

`gen-dev-env.mjs` deliberately never writes `agents/movie-assistant/.env.local` because that file carries the operator's own Anthropic credential, and it names that omission in its output on the same run as the success line — an absent file must be distinguishable from an unconsidered one.

`gen-dev-env.mjs` writes five gitignored env files per run — `frontend/mcm-app/.env.docker` (fully regenerated), `frontend/mcm-app/.env.local`, `frontend/mcm-app/.env.e2e.local`, `mcp-servers/web-api-mcp/.env.local` and `backend/mc-service/.env.local` — and its `syncEnvFile` helper distinguishes two classes of line: `sync` keys (realm-derived credentials and projected backup test credentials) are rewritten on every run so they match the seeded realm, while `defaults` keys are seeded only when absent and never rewritten, so a developer's tuned `RUST_LOG` or redirected `MC_DB_URL` survives a re-run. A create-when-absent behavior (`opts.create`) is opted into per file, which is why the frontend `.env.local` and `backend/mc-service/.env.local` are created but `.env.e2e.local` (whose sync set is only the credential half) is left alone and reported loudly.

`frontend/mcm-app/.env.local` is seeded with host-reachable service URLs (`MONGO_URL`, `BFF_BASE_URL`, `MC_SERVICE_URL`, `KEYCLOAK_URL`, `REDIS_URL`) because a `.env.local` silent on them makes the local integration suites fall back to `.env.docker`'s Docker-internal service names, which no process outside the compose network can resolve — measured 2026-09-20 as `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` failures in a suite whose setup comment already documented that the port came from `.env.local`. The backup test destinations are seeded with both spellings for the same reason: host-side suites reach them on loopback while the BFF container must be given the compose service names.

Because the containerized BFF and the Metro dev loop run against the same BFF Mongo, `gen-dev-env.mjs` reuses `BACKUP_CREDENTIAL_ENC_KEY` and `BACKUP_TICK_SECRET` from `.env.docker` first and `.env.local` second, and re-mints any prior value whose base64-decoded length is not 32 bytes — reusing a wrong-length legacy key would silently preserve the bug it represents, and differing keys between the two files make a value stored correctly under one undecryptable under the other, surfacing later as an authentication failure. `AGENT_CONFIG_ENC_KEY` follows the same 32-byte-base64 validity rule but is reused from `.env.docker` alone (plus `COOKIE_SECRET`); minting it as hex would yield 64 chars that base64-decode to 48 bytes and make every agent-config save fail.

`scripts/__tests__/gen-dev-env.guard.test.mjs` pins the generator's coverage by deriving the set of `.env.local` files documented in `docs/runbooks/` and failing if one is neither written by the generator nor an explicitly reasoned exception (`agents/movie-assistant/.env.local`), and it separately asserts that a deliberately skipped file is named in the generator's output — so a documented file that nothing writes is visible in the guard rather than weeks later in someone's `nx affected`.

Item #552: the `BACKUP_TEST_*` projection out of `stacks/mcm.env` is loud when it has nothing to project — the four key names that are absent or empty are printed (names only, never values) together with the command that back-fills them without rotating anything (`node scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs --stack=mcm`) and the instruction to recreate the `backups` profile containers and re-run the generator; previously the silent filter projected nothing, said nothing, and nine backup-destination integration suites skipped to green.

`scripts/__tests__/gen-dev-env.guard.test.mjs` pins the generator's loudness rules in addition to its coverage: a file the generator deliberately skips (`agents/movie-assistant/.env.local`) must be named in the run's output, and an `mcm.env` missing `BACKUP_TEST_*` keys must cause those key names plus the `gen-dev-secrets.mjs` fix to appear while no stack value is ever echoed. The tests run the real script inside a throwaway mini-repo with synthetic `auth.env` fixtures and the realm check off, so they stay keyless and offline.

A Compose profile is not isolation from interpolation: Compose interpolates every service in an included file at PARSE time regardless of which profiles are selected, so a required `${VAR:?}` inside a profile-gated service aborted `up` for the whole mcm stack — which is why feature 073's backup destinations live in a separate `infrastructure-as-code/docker/backups/compose.yaml` brought up explicitly rather than behind a profile. `REGISTRY_HOST` no longer appears in any dev-stack template: feature 080 replaced the from-source object-store image with upstream `rustfs/rustfs` pulled by digest, so neither the observability object store nor the backup S3 destination interpolates a host at all; the stack file keeps the incident as a comment, and in production the same name is a per-stack Komodo variable that `check-topology-scrub.mjs` keeps out of committed files.

`scripts/__tests__/gen-dev-secrets.guard.test.mjs` pins the item #552 completion rule by copying the real generator into a throwaway mini-repo with a synthetic template: an existing `mcm.env` missing the four `BACKUP_TEST_*` keys gets all four seeded while prior lines are kept byte-for-byte, an empty `<generate:KIND>` key is filled in place (exactly one occurrence, never duplicated), a template-blank fixture (`REGISTRY_HOST`) is not treated as missing so a complete file still reports `up to date` and is not rewritten, and no fixture or minted value is ever printed — only key names.

No Compose stack is profile-gated as a whole: `auth` starts `keycloak-service`, `keycloak-store-postgres` and `keycloak-mailpit` with no profile (Vault needs `vault`), `mcm` starts its test infra — `mc-service-store-mongo` plus its rs-init, `mcm-bff-cache-redis` and `mcm-bff-store-mongo` — with no profile while mc-service needs `app`, the BFF needs `bff-secure`/`bff-nonsecure`, the agent layer needs `agents`, and the Metro-dev gateway `movie-assistant-gateway-metro` is a separate service needing `agents-metro` only (its YAML anchor does not inherit the `agents` profile), and `audit` and `observability` start nothing at all without their profile. Those `profiles:` assignments live in the per-service component compose files, not in the stack aggregators, so a stack's default bring-up is its unprofiled services only.

`scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs` distinguishes credentials from secret-shaped non-credentials by key NAME, not value: a key matching its `PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN|SALT|ENCRYPTION_KEY|_AUTH|REQUIREPASS` pattern is allowlisted when it ends in `_FILE` (a path to a Docker secret), `_USER`, `ACCESS_KEY_ID` (the public half of an S3 pair), `_CLIENT_ID` or `_AUDIENCE`, or is exactly `AGENT_GATEWAY_CLIENT_SECRET` (injected at deploy as `${…:-}`). This is the mechanism that lets those legitimate keys live in tracked compose files without the gate failing.

`up-mcm` is the Nx target that adds `--profile app` itself (`docker compose -p mcm -f …/stacks/mcm.compose.yaml --env-file …/stacks/mcm.env --profile app up -d`), whereas `up-auth` passes no profile flag and brings Keycloak up with the unprofiled trio; so the difference between the stacks' default bring-ups is a property of the target, not of the stack aggregator, and a bare `docker compose -p mcm … up` starts only the unprofiled test-infra stores.

`gen-dev-env.mjs`'s seed-once rule protects what a developer CHOSE, not what the generator itself wrote before a rename: a `.env.local` value byte-equal to a retired generated default — the pre-080 backup S3 internal endpoint and the `BACKUP_ALLOWED_DESTINATION_HOSTS` entry naming the retired backup container — is upgraded in place to the RustFS host, while any other value (including a developer's own endpoint) is left exactly as it is. Without that migration an existing dev box keeps sending the BFF a host that no longer resolves while the fully generated `.env.docker` admits only the new one, and the suites fail on a destination-not-allowed error that reads as a guard bug.

The `mcm` stack's unprofiled bring-up is three stores, and the two Mongo ones are deliberately different shapes: `mc-service-store-mongo` is a single-member replica set (`--replSet rs0`) plus a one-shot `mc-service-store-mongo-rs-init` sidecar that mc-service waits on with `service_completed_successfully`, because mc-service's cascade delete runs inside one multi-document transaction that a standalone `mongod` cannot serve. The sidecar initiates `rs0` with `host: 'localhost:27017'`, which resolves both from the host through the published port and from mc-service in Docker, which connects with `directConnection=true` and so never chases the member announcement.

Bringing the movie-store Mongo up with a bare `docker run` instead of the stack can initialise the replica set with the Docker-internal hostname, after which host-side `cargo test` fails with "No such host is known" while the container itself looks healthy; the documented repair is an `rs.reconfig(…, { force: true })` naming `localhost:27017`. A failed or interrupted integration run also leaves `mc_test_*` databases behind (one crash left 31) — harmless but accumulating, which is why the cleanup command anchors its regex on the 32-hex suffix so the real `mc_db` can never match.

`mcm-bff-store-mongo` is a plain standalone `mongod` — no `--replSet`, no `directConnection`, no rs-init sidecar — because the BFF store does single-document upserts only and needs no transactions. It publishes on host port 27018 so it cannot collide with the movie store's 27017, and it exists as a separate store because the BFF must not reach across a service boundary into mc-service's database.

`mcm-bff-cache-redis` starts with no profile alongside the two Mongo stores, and the BFF's login path reads it with no typed wrapper around the first call: with Redis down, `/login` returns a bare 500 "Authentication failed" rather than a typed infrastructure error, so Redis is the first thing to check when login breaks locally.

MongoDB 9.0 runs `mongod` as uid 1000 where 8.0.8 ran it as 998, so a volume written by the older image is foreign-owned and 9.0 refuses to start on it with `Unable to read the storage engine metadata file ... storage.bson` (`FileNotOpen`, measured 2026-10-20) — and nothing in the image fixes it, since its own entrypoint started as root does not drop privileges. Both Mongo services therefore start as root only to re-own `/data/db` once (logging `mongo-data-owner: re-owning /data/db to mongod (uid …)`, and skipping `.mongodb`, which is mongosh's own client-log directory under `HOME=/data/db`), then `setpriv` down to the image's `mongod` user before `mongod` runs, so `mongod` itself never runs as root.

The mongo-data-owner wrapper is guarded so a future image move cannot brick a populated volume: `scripts/__tests__/mongo-data-owner.guard.test.mjs` asserts every MongoDB service that mounts `/data/db` in the four Mongo-bearing compose files starts as `user: "0:0"` with the `sh -c` wrapper and hands off to `mongod`, that the wrapper script text is identical across all four files, and — by executing it against stubs — that it chowns then `setpriv`s when root with foreign-owned data, chowns nothing but still drops privileges when already owned, and execs unchanged when not root. Going back to 8.0.8 on a volume 9.0 has already run on is not supported; a dump is restored onto a fresh volume instead.

mc-service's two infrastructure dependencies fail asymmetrically, and the difference is the diagnostic: an unreachable `MC_DB_URL` is a hard startup failure, because `main()` connects and creates all indexes before it builds the router or binds, while an unreachable Keycloak is not — the service starts, `/health` answers, and every protected request is rejected with 401.

The mc-service integration harness's configuration panic names the fix, not just the failure: it reports the missing configuration, the command that supplies it (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs`), the runbook section, and that the failure is a CONFIGURATION failure distinct from the `http_authz_test::*` cases that genuinely need the local replica-set MongoDB — so the item #227 cause and the real infrastructure requirement stay apart at the moment of failure.

`node verify/verify-fresh-realm-seed.mjs` is the end-to-end assertion for the whole fresh-box path: by default it provisions from scratch (wipe the volume → both generators → `pnpm nx up-auth infrastructure-as-code`) and then proves the seed with a real ROPC token grant — `e2e-test-user` authenticating against `mcm-bff-test` with the minted password and client secret — which only succeeds if the realm, its clients and `stacks/auth.env` are all coherent; `--assert-only` skips provisioning and asserts against an already-running auth stack.

The realm-wipe recovery only works if the containers mounting the volume are force-removed first: `docker compose down --volumes` does not remove an `external: true` volume and `docker volume rm` fails silently while a container still references it, so the wipe no-ops and Postgres keeps the password it was initialised with — after which Keycloak dies with `password authentication failed for user "keycloak"` and the realm never imports.

The `gen-dev-env.guard` tests exercise item #395's refusal path without a live realm, by running the real generator against a stub Keycloak on loopback: a 401 from the stub must leave an existing `.env.e2e.local` holding the working value byte-for-byte intact, write nothing else, exit non-zero, name the stale credential, quote the realm's own `unauthorized_client`, print no secret value, and never emit the `realm-secret == BFF-secret == E2E-cred` claim. The same guard pins the item #227 file's behaviour from the other side — an absent `backend/mc-service/.env.local` is created with the documented local values, an existing one keeps a tuned `RUST_LOG`, a redirected `MC_DB_URL` and unrelated keys, and a file that exists but lacks `MC_DB_URL` has it appended.

The dev compose agent gateway is Ollama-only — `MODEL_PROVIDER=ollama` with `SUPERVISOR_MODEL` defaulting to `qwen2.5` and `SPECIALIST_MODEL` to `qwen2.5:32b`, reaching host Ollama at `host.docker.internal:11434` — so the host must be serving those models, and the graph takes roughly 20–40 s to build before the gateway's health endpoint answers. The separate `movie-assistant-gateway-metro` service declares `profiles: [agents-metro]` explicitly because YAML anchors do not merge `profiles`, so it never starts under `--profile agents`.
